subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm designing an armored hauler truck as a static TypeScript model — six wheels, a cab, armored plates, a sealed cargo pod, glowing strips, a turret, antenna, and lights, keeping it joint-free for simplicity.

I'm laying out the exact dimensions: a 9m-long, 3m-wide chassis with wheel axle positions, a steel frame box, and an extruded cab profile that slopes into a windshield and nose shape.

For the finish, I'll use panelled metal from the clockwork kit with glow effects, and place a dark cyan windshield decal plane angled along the slope between the cab roof and nose, positioning it precisely with a normal offset so it doesn't clip the body.

Now I'm adding side windows as small textured planes facing outward on the cab sides, then working out the cargo pod geometry as a horizontal lathe-generated capsule positioned above the chassis, sizing its radius and length to sit cleanly on the frame without intersecting the cab.

Shaping the pod outline, adding hazard striping rings and cradle strap bands as separate thin lathe rings in contrasting colors, plus a glowing rear hatch seal detail.

I'm planning to decal the biohazard texture onto the pod surface, positioning it to project outward so it reads correctly from either viewing side, then moving on to the side skirts and armor plating near the wheel wells.

Checking wheel outer positions against chassis and cab widths to make sure wheels tuck in properly beside the cab without clipping, then adding fender boxes above the wheels sized to clear the wheel tops.

Now I'm defining the wheel assembly: dark tire cylinders, steel rim cylinders, and a thin glowing cyan ring for accent, looped across all eight wheels on the four axles. Then I'm adding rear details like bumper and red glowing taillights, plus front details including a bull bar wedge and a cyan headlight stripe mounted on the cab's front face.

I'm also designing a roof turret with a hex base, twin gun barrels, a sensor dome, antenna rods with glowing tips, and an amber light bar, along with exhaust stacks positioned behind the cab with glowing tips, working out their placement relative to the tapering pod front.

Now I'm figuring out the pod and chassis span, placing a rear bumper and hatch door with a tapered end cap disc, adding an emblem texture facing backward, and checking that the hatch disc sits properly against the chassis rear without bad overlap. I'm also starting on under-glow neon strips running along the chassis sides.

Next I'm adding cyan glow rods on the cab edges, amber seal rings at the pod joints, container lock handles, and side battery boxes mounted between the axles, while sketching out axle positions for front steering and rear wheels.

For textures I'm planning out around six SVG decals: windshield, side window, pod emblem, hatch emblem, grille, and a "CONVOY 07" door decal, alongside metal paint materials.

I'm defining a custom hull paint by mixing dark navy tones with mottling and grime that intensifies lower on the body, plus a separate riveted panel paint for the pod. I'm also sketching out helper functions for boxes, wheels, and glow effects, along with how cylinder geometry gets oriented along different axes.

Since this model is static, I can skip joints entirely and focus on extruding the cab shape from a polygon outline defined in z-y space -- tracing the hood slope, windshield angle, and roofline points to get the proportions right.

Still placing windshield geometry... now I'm working out the side window planes for the cab, positioning them against the roof slope, then placing door decal text like "HX-07" on the side panel.

For the mirrored side, I'm flipping the facing direction so the texture still reads correctly from outside. Then I'm adding roof details: a cyberpunk-style light bar with magenta/cyan boxes instead of standard amber, and a rear turret assembly with a hex base, a head box, and twin rotating barrel cylinders mounted near the back of the roof.

Checking placement so nothing clips oddly — the turret sits clear of the windshield, the sensor pod on the cab roof clears the turret head, and I'm positioning the rear tail lights as red glowing boxes near the back bumper.

Now I'm shaping a front ram/bumper using an extruded wedge profile angled downward toward the ground, keeping it dark hazard-colored and making sure the lowest points stay at wheel height so nothing floats. I'm also adding cyan headlight boxes slanted on the cab front near the ram.

Positioning the grille plane just in front of the hood, then adding simple fender boxes over each wheel axle to cover the overlap with the chassis top. I'm also planning angular armor plates on the cab doors using an extruded polygon offset outward from the cab sides.

Settling on x=1.32 for the door decal plane. For the pod, I'm positioning the emblem decal and figuring out strap placements along the z-axis so they don't overlap the decal's span, trying positions around -3.4 to 0.3.

Now I'm defining the lathe outline for the strap rings using radius/height coordinate pairs, and sketching out box positions for a support cradle between the pod and chassis.

Next I'm setting up hazard stripe paint for the rear bumper and ram top using diagonal black-and-yellow striping, then planning roof antennas as thin glowing rods at the rear cab corners with tip spheres, before moving on to the satellite dish.

Adding dish geometry and pod rear hatch disc...

I need to reposition the underglow strip to avoid colliding with the wheels—keeping it between axles rather than spanning the full length. I'm also adding a glowing magenta underbody plank beneath the chassis center, plus side skirt armor pieces, and now setting up the wheel positions along the z-axis.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Now I'm sketching out the color palette and paint functions for the hull material, keeping colors under budget while defining a custom paint that mixes tones based on noise and surface normals.

Designing SVG decals...

Now I'm tuning glow intensities on each decal—windshield at low strength, hatch a bit stronger, skipping the emblem glow entirely—while making sure the decal textures use alpha testing for clean cutouts on the lathe geometry. For the turret, I'm sketching a hexagonal lathe base with a tapered profile and a small box-shaped head mounted above it.

I'm positioning the sensor eye as a glowing cyan box on the turret front, and placing twin barrels as steel rods extending forward with glowing muzzle tips, double-checking that their length stops short of the windshield geometry. I'm also working out the exhaust stacks as cylinders mounted at the rear corners of the cab, making sure their placement lines up with the cab's rear face and the pod's tapering radius near its end cap.

I'm refining the pod's tapering profile, adding small details like a glowing amber seal strip along the top seam and considering thin rib bands near the pod's front and rear ends for surface detail, while deciding to skip extra warning beacons to keep things simple.

I'm also planning rear-view camera pods mounted on either side of the cab with mounting arms and cyan lenses, double-checking that the overall height with antennas stays around 4.3 units, and setting up compact helper functions for generating boxes and cylinders to keep the construction code concise.

Now I'm drafting a build sheet comment under 40 lines, adding a glow helper that works on flat-colored or textured parts, planning a windshield decal using a plane geometry with texture, and working out the grille's placement as a flat panel centered on the front face of the cab.

For the ram/bumper, I'm deciding to simplify by using a box shape sized roughly 2.4 by 0.7 by 0.45 positioned at the front, plus a thin top plate for hazard stripe paint, rather than extruding a sloped wedge profile. I settle on a grille plane positioned at height 0.95 with a 0.55 height to fit the ram box.

Now I'm working through the lathe-based pod geometry, checking that the pod's bottom radius of 1.3 clears the chassis top at 1.25, then adding a ring helper function and positioning door plates and window panes symmetrically on each side of the cab using mirrored x-offsets.
